title: Pinchas son of Abba (Shmuel’s father)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Shmuel’s brother, and the two brothers married two sisters, as related in [Sanhedrin 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.28b.21). In [Bekhorot 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.39a.5-7), Pinchas, Mar Shmuel’s brother, asked Shmuel a question that Shmuel could not answer. Shmuel applied to him the saying, “The lame have taken plunder.” Although Pinchas was not especially sharp, he asked a question Shmuel could not answer.[^1][^2]

[Moed Katan 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.18a.2-3) relates that Pinchas became a mourner. Shmuel came to comfort him and saw that his nails were long. “Why haven’t you trimmed them?” Shmuel asked. Pinchas replied, “If you were a mourner, would you treat it so lightly?”
The remark proved to be “like an error issuing from a ruler,” and Shmuel became a mourner.[^3]

notes.text: The heading identifies **Abba** as Shmuel’s father; Pinchas is Shmuel’s brother.

The saying alludes to [Isaiah 33:23](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.33.23). Here *piseḥim* means “the lame,” not the tractate Pesachim. Hyman gives פסחים בזו בז. In the [Romm–Vilna printing of Bekhorot 39a](https://manuscripts.sefaria.org/vilna-romm/Bekhorot_39a.jpg), the Gemara reads פסחים בזו (בוז), while Rashi on the same page has פסחים בזזו בז. Sefaria’s vocalized William Davidson text also has פסחים בזזו בז, matching Isaiah.

“Like an error issuing from a ruler” alludes to [Ecclesiastes 10:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Ecclesiastes.10.5). In the Talmudic account, Pinchas’s remark is treated as an inadvertent utterance that came true in Shmuel’s own bereavement.
